key_insight: For a fixed physical system, the input-to-response operator is independent of the input probability law, enabling potential reuse of learned operators across uncertainty distributions.
engineering_relevance: Mechanics surrogates may predict response fields and statistics under changed uncertainty laws without retraining, provided training adequately covers the relevant inputs.
method: Establish law invariance under complete, invertible coordinate transformations.
Develop Fourier, fixed-reference polynomial-chaos, and FEM transfer formulations.
Approximate deterministic operators with neural models and test cross-law generalization.
evidence_signal: Analytical and finite-element benchmarks examine cross-law generalization, training-distribution effects, stochastic excitation, and prediction of response fields and statistics.
watch_item: Law invariance does not guarantee surrogate accuracy outside training coverage, and low-probability response events remain difficult to estimate accurately.
